series.subtitle: Yoreh Deah with Rabbi Leibtag
series.description: Shiurim covering Yoreh Deah — beginning with Siman 95 (Nat Bar Nat) and continuing through Siman 123 (yayin nesech). Building on the previous zman's coverage of basar b'chalav.

shiurim.title: Introduction to Nat Bar Nat
shiurim.hebrewTitle: נותן טעם בר נותן טעם — מבוא
shiurim.description: Opening shiur of the zman. Reviews basar b'chalav fundamentals (hana'ah, achilah, bishul), introduces nat bar nat (נותן טעם בר נותן טעם), surveys the Gemara in Chullin (דגים שעלו בקערה), Tosafos in Zevachim, and a three-way machlokes Rishonim: Rivan/Rashi, Sefer HaTerumah/Rosh, and Rambam. Covers Shulchan Aruch Siman 95, seifim 1–2, and the Rema's chumra. Concludes with practical shailos on ice cream (Dayan Weiss / Minchas Yitzchak) and the pareve cake question.
notesSummary: The Gemara in Chullin (111b) debates whether hot parve fish placed on a fleishig plate may be eaten with dairy — Rav forbids, Shmuel permits.
נ"ט בר נ"ט (nat bar nat): flavor that transfers twice is sufficiently weakened and does not create a basar b'chalav prohibition.
Three-way machlokes Rishonim: Rivan/Rashi (only allows placement, not cooking), Sefer HaTerumah (allows cooking in pot but not frying in pan), Rambam (allows even frying).
S"A (95:1) rules like the Rambam — parve food cooked in a clean fleishig ben-yomo pot may be eaten with dairy.
Rama is machmir: le'chatchilla one may not add dairy to parve food cooked in a ben-yomo fleishig pot, but bedi'eved it is permitted.
Practical: "DE" (Dairy Equipment) labeling — for Sephardim fully parve, for Ashkenazim depends on whether machines are ben-yomo. Minchas Yitzchak rules a hechsher should follow the stricter view.
Parve cake baked for dessert in an eino ben-yomo fleishig pan may be eaten with dairy coffee (Minchas Yitzchak / Minchas Sefer).

quiz.q: What is the core principle of נ"ט בר נ"ט (nat bar nat)?
options: Flavor transferred twice is sufficiently weakened and does not create a basar b'chalav prohibition
Any absorbed flavor renders food permanently non-kosher
Only flavor absorbed within the last 24 hours is halachically significant
Flavor can only transfer through cooking, not through contact
quiz.explanation: נ"ט בר נ"ט means "flavor that imparts flavor" — when meat flavor transfers from meat to a pot, and then from the pot to parve food, it has been weakened twice. Shmuel (Chullin 111b) rules this double-transferred flavor does not create a sufficient fusion of meat and dairy to forbid the food.

quiz.q: According to the S"A (Siman 95, Seif 1), parve pasta cooked in a clean fleishig ben-yomo pot:
options: May not be eaten with dairy under any circumstances
May be eaten with dairy
May only be eaten with dairy if there is shishim against the absorbed meat flavor
Must be treated as fully fleishig
quiz.explanation: The S"A follows the Rambam's opinion that parve food cooked in a clean fleishig pot is permitted with dairy. The meat flavor undergoes a double transfer (nat bar nat) — from meat to pot, then pot to food — rendering it too weakened to create a basar b'chalav prohibition.

quiz.q: The Rama rules: if dairy was already added to parve food that was cooked in a ben-yomo fleishig pot, the food is:
options: Completely forbidden
Permitted — bedi'eved it may be eaten
Forbidden unless there is shishim
The subject of a dispute between the Taz and the Shach
quiz.explanation: The Rama follows the Issur V'Heter — le'chatchilla one should not intentionally add dairy to parve food cooked in a ben-yomo fleishig pot, but since in principle we hold nat bar nat is permitted, if dairy was already added the food is permitted. The chumra is a harchaka (safeguard), not a core prohibition.

quiz.q: What does the kosher symbol "DE" (Dairy Equipment) signify?
options: The product contains actual dairy ingredients
The product is 100% parve for all opinions
The product was made on dairy equipment — for Ashkenazim it may not be intentionally added to meat le'chatchilla if the machines were ben-yomo
The product was accidentally contaminated with a trace of dairy
quiz.explanation: DE means the parve product was manufactured on dairy machinery. For Sephardim it is fully parve. For Ashkenazim it depends on whether the machines were ben-yomo (used for dairy within 24 hours) — if so, the Rama's chumra applies and the product should not be intentionally mixed with meat le'chatchilla.

quiz.q: The Minchas Yitzchak (Dayan Weiss) ruled regarding parve ice cream made in eino ben-yomo dairy equipment and labeled "parve":
options: Completely correct — such labeling is fully permitted
Permitted for Sephardim but not for Ashkenazim
Erroneous — a hechsher implies the food may be eaten with meat, and the stricter opinion (Chachmas Adam) should be followed
Permitted as long as the ingredients list discloses the dairy equipment
quiz.explanation: The Minchas Yitzchak ruled that labeling such ice cream as "parve" is erroneous because a hechsher implies the food may be freely eaten with meat. The Chachmas Adam holds one may not cook parve food in an eino ben-yomo pot with intent to eat it with the opposite food. Therefore, a hechsher should follow the stricter opinion and not label it simply as parve.

shiurim.title: Rav Moshe on Ben Yomo Pots and Davar Charif
shiurim.hebrewTitle: פסקי הרב משה פיינשטיין — כלי בן יומו ודבר חריף
shiurim.description: Continues nat bar nat discussion through the lens of Rav Moshe Feinstein's teshuva (Igros Moshe YD 1:11). Explores the Rema's chumra on cooking parve in ben yomo pots with intent for dairy/meat, contrasts Taz vs. Shach on כדי אוכלן בכותח, analyzes davar charif (onions, garlic) and their ability to reawaken taste. Reviews Pischei Teshuva on broccoli-and-cheese shaila, the machlokes Pri Megadim vs. Pnei Aryeh on nat bar nat through food vs. keilim, and the Chavos Daas's middle approach.
notesSummary: Rav Moshe (Igros Moshe YD 1:11) rules leniently: one may deliberately fry fish in a dairy ben-yomo pot to serve on fleishig dishes.
The Aruch HaShulchan permits heating cold parve food (cooked in a fleishig pot) inside a dairy ben-yomo pot — the nat bar nat flavor in the food cannot forbid the dairy pot.
Eating two nat bar nat foods together is permitted: e.g., parve eggs from a dairy pan with fleishig potatoes from Shabbos.
Davar charif (sharp food: onion, garlic, radish): its sharpness awakens and reactivates absorbed pagum flavor — the nat bar nat leniency does NOT apply.
Onions fried in an eino ben-yomo fleishig pan may NOT be eaten with dairy — the onion's sharpness "wakes up" the weakened meat flavor.
The Pischei Teshuva discusses broccoli cooked with cheese — may it be placed on a fleishig plate? The Pri Megadim vs. Pnei Aryeh dispute on nat bar nat through food vs. keilim.
The Chavos Daas's middle approach: nat bar nat through keilim (vessels) is always permitted, but through food vs. keilim is disputed.

quiz.q: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 1:11) rules regarding deliberately frying fish in a dairy ben-yomo pot to serve on fleishig dishes:
options: Completely forbidden
Permitted le'chatchilla
Permitted only in a case of great need (sha'as hadechak)
Permitted only for Sephardim
quiz.explanation: Rav Moshe rules leniently that one may deliberately fry fish in a dairy ben-yomo pot and serve it on fleishig dishes. He argues that the Rama was only machmir about adding dairy to the food itself, but not about serving it on a plate of the opposite type — and even the Chachmas Adam would agree in this case.

quiz.q: What makes a davar charif (e.g., onion, garlic) halachically distinct from other parve foods?
options: It is classified as fleishig by nature
It cannot absorb taste from utensils at all
Its sharpness awakens and strengthens absorbed pagum (weakened) flavor in utensils, so the nat bar nat leniency does not apply
It requires a special bracha before eating
quiz.explanation: A davar charif has the halachic property of reactivating pagum flavor — its sharpness "wakes up" the otherwise-weakened meat flavor absorbed in a pot or knife. This means that when onions are fried in an eino ben-yomo fleishig pan, the meat flavor in the onions is as potent as if the pan were ben-yomo, and they may not be eaten with dairy.

quiz.q: Parve eggs fried in a dairy ben-yomo pan, eaten together with leftover fleishig potatoes from Shabbos (cooked in a ben-yomo fleishig pot):
options: Forbidden — both absorbed opposing flavors
Permitted — eating one nat bar nat with another nat bar nat is allowed
Permitted only according to the S"A, not the Rama
Forbidden unless there is shishim across the combined dish
quiz.explanation: Both the S"A and Rama agree that two nat bar nat foods (one from a dairy vessel, one from a fleishig vessel) may be eaten together. The concern of nat bar nat applies only when the food is eaten together with actual dairy or meat — not when two nat bar nat foods are mixed with each other, since each food's flavor is already twice-weakened.

quiz.q: According to the Aruch HaShulchan, may cold parve spaghetti (made in a ben-yomo fleishig pot) be heated inside a dairy ben-yomo pot?
options: No — direct contact of two opposing ben-yomo flavors in a hot pot creates basar b'chalav
Yes — the meat flavor in the spaghetti is already nat bar nat and cannot forbid the dairy pot
Only if the dairy pot is eino ben-yomo
Only bedi'eved, but not le'chatchilla
quiz.explanation: The Aruch HaShulchan argues against the Taz and permits heating parve food (cooked in a ben-yomo fleishig pot) inside a dairy ben-yomo pot. His reasoning: the meat flavor in the parve spaghetti is already nat bar nat (twice-transferred), so even when it contacts the dairy flavor from the hot pot, it cannot create a real basar b'chalav prohibition.

quiz.q: The Chavos Daas's position in the debate between the Pri Megadim and the Pnei Aryeh on nat bar nat:
options: Agrees entirely with the Pri Megadim that nat bar nat through food vs. keilim is always permitted
Agrees entirely with the Pnei Aryeh that nat bar nat through food vs. keilim is always forbidden
Takes a middle approach: nat bar nat through keilim (vessel-to-vessel) is always permitted, but through food vs. keilim is disputed
Rules that the entire concept of nat bar nat only applies to fish, not to other parve foods
quiz.explanation: The Chavos Daas offers a middle position between the Pri Megadim (lenient) and Pnei Aryeh (strict): when flavor transfers vessel-to-vessel (kli to kli), the nat bar nat leniency applies fully. But when the transfer is from food to vessel or vessel to food, the application is disputed. This distinction helps explain many practical shailos about mixing nat bar nat foods.

shiurim.title: Fish and Meat: Danger, Bitul, and Washing Dishes
shiurim.hebrewTitle: דגים ובשר — סכנה, ביטול, ושטיפת כלים
shiurim.description: Recording was unavailable for this shiur — notes are the primary resource. Covers section E: the prohibition and medical danger of eating fish and meat together (tzara'as; Gemara Pesachim 76b), the Magen Avraham's leniency that the danger may no longer apply, bitul b'shishim for fish-and-meat mixtures, and practical halachos (kiddush, Japanese restaurants, Worcestershire sauce). Begins section F: the washing-dishes sugya — accidentally rinsing dairy utensils in a fleishig pot.
notesSummary: The Gemara (Pesachim 76b) teaches that eating fish and meat together causes bad breath and tzara'as — hence the prohibition.
S"A (YD 116:2): one may not eat fish and meat together. Rama: one should also avoid baking them in the same oven, but bedi'eved it is permitted.
Magen Avraham (OC 173:1): today the danger may no longer apply due to changed medical circumstances — used as a lenient tziruf by some acharonim.
Consensus of acharonim: fish may be cooked in clean fleishig pots le'chatchilla; a fish-and-meat mixture is batel b'shishim (though some are stringent).
Worcestershire sauce: if anchovies are not batel b'shishim → requires OU-Fish label. If batel → plain OU is sufficient (Rav Belsky).
At a kiddush or Japanese restaurant: most are lenient to place fish and meat on the same table, but one should change utensils between eating them.

Washing dishes: Sefer HaTerumah — accidentally rinsing clean dairy utensils in a hot fleishig pot: if both are ben-yomo, everything is forbidden. Rosh: permitted if all utensils are clean. S"A follows the Rosh; Rama follows Sefer HaTerumah.

quiz.q: What health concern underlies the prohibition of eating fish and meat together?
options: Allergic reactions between fish proteins and meat proteins
Concern for bad breath and tzara'as (a serious skin affliction)
Risk of food poisoning from improper cooking temperatures
Concern that the meat would become non-kosher
quiz.explanation: The Gemara in Pesachim (76b) records that baking fish and meat together — where only their aromas mix — causes bad breath and tzara'as. The Taz (YD 116) extrapolates that cooking or eating them together, which causes a more direct fusion, is certainly forbidden on these grounds of danger (sekhana).

quiz.q: Fish and meat were accidentally baked together in separate, uncovered pans in the same oven. According to the Rama, what is the status of the food?
options: Completely forbidden — their aromas fused
Le'chatchilla forbidden due to richa (aroma), but bedi'eved the food is permitted
Completely permitted since they were in separate pans
Forbidden only if the oven was ben-yomo
quiz.explanation: The Rama rules that fish and meat should not be baked in the same oven even in separate pans because of richa (aroma mixing). However, if they were accidentally baked together in separate, uncovered pans, the food is permitted bedi'eved — since only aromas, not flavors, mixed. If covered, the Rama would forbid even bedi'eved.

quiz.q: Rav Belsky (OU) rules regarding Worcestershire sauce that contains anchovies not batel b'shishim:
options: The sauce cannot receive any kosher certification
A plain OU symbol is sufficient since most poskim permit fish-meat mixtures
An "OU-Fish" label is required so that those machmir about fish-meat mixtures will know not to use it with meat
The fish must be removed before the sauce can be certified
quiz.explanation: Rav Belsky rules that when the fish content is not batel b'shishim, an "OU-Fish" label is required. This alerts anyone who is machmir about fish-meat mixtures not to use it with meat. When the anchovies are batel b'shishim, a plain OU may be used, relying on both the majority opinion permitting bitul for fish-meat mixtures and the Magen Avraham's leniency.

quiz.q: According to the Magen Avraham (OC 173:1), the prohibition of mixing fish and meat today:
options: Applies as strictly as ever — the Gemara's ruling does not change with time
May no longer apply, as the medical danger may have changed over time and location
Applies only when fish and meat are cooked together, not eaten separately
Applies only for Sephardim, not for Ashkenazim
quiz.explanation: The Magen Avraham notes that the original concern may have been localized to certain times or places, and the medical danger may no longer exist today. Later poskim disagree on how far this leniency extends — some (Chayyei HaLevi) say only not washing between fish and meat, while others (Divrei Malki'el) permit even eating them together, used as a lenient tziruf.

quiz.q: Clean dairy utensils were accidentally rinsed in a clean, ben-yomo fleishig pot on the fire. According to the Rama, the status of the utensils and pot is:
options: Everything is permitted since all utensils were clean
Everything is forbidden
The water is forbidden but the utensils are permitted
Permitted bedi'eved since the flavor is nat bar nat
quiz.explanation: The Rama follows the Sefer HaTerumah: when clean dairy utensils (ben-yomo) are rinsed in a clean, ben-yomo fleishig pot with heat, everything is forbidden — the pot, water, and dairy utensils. The Taz explains: either the utensils directly touch the pot (direct flavor fusion), or the flavors meet in the water before either is fully weakened, creating basar b'chalav. The S"A (following the Rosh) permits this since both flavors are nat bar nat in the water.

shiurim.title: Washing Dishes
shiurim.description: Covers the halachos of washing dishes — accidentally rinsing dairy utensils in a fleishig pot and vice versa, continuing from Shiur 3. Analyzes the machlokes between the Sefer HaTerumah and the Rosh (quoted in the Tur), the Shulchan Aruch and Rema's rulings in Siman 95:3, and practical applications of Nosein Taam Lifgam.
